messages:
ops-bot: ALERT — p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in router-prod (us-east-1)
ops-bot: metric: p99=3.2s (SLO 1.5s), p95=320ms. incident auto-created INC-1769954321. graphs: https://grafana.redwood/incoming/1769954321
alyssa: paging @infra-oncall — seeing massive p99, can you jump in?
infra-oncall: oncall here, looking now. pulling p99/p95 and per-host.
mike: i see streaming stalls and queueing on a subset of router pods in us-east-1-lb-group-7. p95 fine, p99 blown out.
sana: any recent routing/deploy changes? i can see a config push ~5m ago: traffic-policy "adaptive-weight" applied to router-policy-3.
jordan: yep that was a canary from deploy-bot at 1769954280 — PR: https://git.redwood/pr/8345 — added region affinity + adaptive-steering logic.
alyssa: sounds like a hot-partition: can we get per-backend connection counts?
infra-oncall: running:
```
kubectl exec router-ctrl -- curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep backend_conn
```
infra-oncall: result: backend_conn{shard="s7"}=3421, backend_conn{shard="s1"}=124, s2=98 ... s7 is huge.
mike: that's the hot shard. also seeing weight-shedding 502s from the overloaded backends.
sana: adaptive-weight probably created a positive feedback loop: higher recent p99 -> policy pushes weight to supposedly faster backends but ended up concentrating into s7.
alyssa: mitigation plan: rollback policy to static weights and drain the hot shard. infra, can you rollback now?
infra-oncall: rolling back: `deploy-bot rollback router-policy-3 --to=rev-612` — started.
deploy-bot: rollback job started (job id 6821). ETA ~45s. :hourglass_flowing_sand: \
jordan: temporarily caps set: `curl -XPOST https://admin.router/policy/3/set?cap=0.2` — applied to avoid reconcentration.
ops-bot: status update: p99 trending down 3.2s -> 1.9s since rollback started.
mike: initiating drain of s7: `kubectl annotate node s7-marker cordon=true` then evict pods. starting evictions now.
infra-oncall: evictions in progress. note: some long-lived streaming sessions; eviction set to graceful with 60s.
cs-ega: customer impact summary: ~4.3% of requests breached SLO in the last 10m, primarily from us-east. top affected customers: acme-inc, betaapp. CS contacting them now.
alyssa: good catch. also check upstream: did eu region have an issue that pushed traffic east?
mike: eu had transient 503s ~6m ago from edge-proxy which caused global steering to favor us-east. that influx then got misdistributed inside us-east.
infra-oncall: rollback job 6821 finished SUCCESS. p99 stabilized at ~1.2s. evictions complete.
jordan: opening postmortem doc. immediate action items: disable adaptive-weight until we implement weight caps and per-shard circuit breakers; add distribution metrics; add canary tests for oscillation.
sana: also add guardrail to canary (fail canary if per-shard weight variance > 0.3) and integration test in canary harness.
alyssa: handing off to next oncall @infra-oncall. i'll update the incident doc with timeline and customer impact. follow-ups assigned, will keep CS looped. ETA for customer follow-up 1.5h.
ops-bot: Incident moved to monitoring state and follow-up ticket INC-1769954321 created. :white_check_mark:
